1CO.12.31.t: But eagerly desire the greater gifts. And now I will show you the most excellent way.
s: But eagerly desire the greater gifts.
And now I will show you the most excellent way.

1CO.13.1.t: If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I am only a ringing gong or a clanging cymbal.
s: If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I am only a ringing gong or a clanging cymbal.

1CO.13.2.t: If I have the gift of prophecy and can fathom all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have absolute faith so as to move mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.
s: If I have the gift of prophecy and can fathom all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have absolute faith so as to move mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.

1CO.13.3.t: If I give all I possess to the poor and exult in the surrender of my body, but have not love, I gain nothing.
s: If I give all I possess to the poor and exult in the surrender of my body, but have not love, I gain nothing.

1CO.13.4.t: Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.
s: Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.

1CO.13.5.t: It is not rude, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no account of wrongs.
s: It is not rude, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no account of wrongs.

1CO.13.6.t: Love takes no pleasure in evil, but rejoices in the truth.
s: Love takes no pleasure in evil, but rejoices in the truth.

1CO.13.7.t: It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
s: It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.

1CO.13.8.t: Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will cease; where there are tongues, they will be restrained; where there is knowledge, it will be dismissed.
s: Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will cease; where there are tongues, they will be restrained; where there is knowledge, it will be dismissed.

1CO.13.9.t: For we know in part and we prophesy in part,
s: For we know in part and we prophesy in part,

1CO.13.10.t: but when the perfect comes, the partial passes away.
s: but when the perfect comes, the partial passes away.

1CO.13.11.t: When I was a child, I talked like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I set aside childish ways.
s: When I was a child, I talked like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I set aside childish ways.

1CO.13.12.t: Now we see but a dim reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face. Now I know in part; then I shall know fully, even as I am fully known.
s: Now we see but a dim reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face. Now I know in part; then I shall know fully, even as I am fully known.

1CO.13.13.t: And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love; but the greatest of these is love.
s: And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love; but the greatest of these is love.

1JN.4.7.t: Beloved, let us love one another, because love comes from God. Everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.
s: Beloved, let us love one another, because love comes from God. Everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.

1JN.4.8.t: Whoever does not love does not know God, because God is love.
s: Whoever does not love does not know God, because God is love.

1JN.4.9.t: This is how God’s love was revealed among us: God sent His one and only Son into the world, so that we might live through Him.
s: This is how God’s love was revealed among us: God sent His one and only Son into the world, so that we might live through Him.

1JN.4.10.t: And love consists in this: not that we loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins.
s: And love consists in this: not that we loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins.

1JN.4.11.t: Beloved, if God so loved us, we also ought to love one another.
s: Beloved, if God so loved us, we also ought to love one another.

1JN.4.12.t: No one has ever seen God; but if we love one another, God remains in us, and His love is perfected in us.
s: No one has ever seen God; but if we love one another, God remains in us, and His love is perfected in us.

1PE.4.7.t: The end of all things is near. Therefore be clear-minded and sober, so that you can pray.
s: The end of all things is near. Therefore be clear-minded and sober, so that you can pray.

1PE.4.8.t: Above all, love one another deeply, because love covers over a multitude of sins.
s: Above all, love one another deeply, because love covers over a multitude of sins.

1PE.4.9.t: Show hospitality to one another without complaining.
s: Show hospitality to one another without complaining.

1PE.4.10.t: As good stewards of the manifold grace of God, each of you should use whatever gift he has received to serve one another.
s: As good stewards of the manifold grace of God, each of you should use whatever gift he has received to serve one another.

1PE.4.11.t: If anyone speaks, he should speak as one conveying the words of God. If anyone serves, he should serve with the strength God provides, so that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen.
s: If anyone speaks, he should speak as one conveying the words of God. If anyone serves, he should serve with the strength God provides, so that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen.

1TH.5.11.t: Therefore encourage and build one another up, just as you are already doing.
s: Therefore encourage and build one another up, just as you are already doing.

1TH.5.12.t: But we ask you, brothers, to acknowledge those who work diligently among you, who preside over you in the Lord and give you instruction.
s: But we ask you, brothers, to acknowledge those who work diligently among you, who preside over you in the Lord and give you instruction.

1TH.5.13.t: In love, hold them in highest regard because of their work. Live in peace with one another.
s: In love, hold them in highest regard because of their work. Live in peace with one another.

1TH.5.14.t: And we urge you, brothers, to admonish the unruly, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, and be patient with everyone.
s: And we urge you, brothers, to admonish the unruly, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, and be patient with everyone.

1TH.5.15.t: Make sure that no one repays evil for evil. Always pursue what is good for one another and for all people.
s: Make sure that no one repays evil for evil. Always pursue what is good for one another and for all people.
Command and teach these things.

1TI.4.12.t: Let no one despise your youth, but set an example for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.
s: Let no one despise your youth, but set an example for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.

1TI.4.13.t: Until I come, devote yourself to the public reading of Scripture, to exhortation, and to teaching.
s: Until I come, devote yourself to the public reading of Scripture, to exhortation, and to teaching.

1TI.4.14.t: Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which was given you through the prophecy spoken over you at the laying on of the hands of the elders.
s: Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which was given you through the prophecy spoken over you at the laying on of the hands of the elders.

1TI.4.15.t: Be diligent in these matters and absorbed in them, so that your progress will be evident to all.
s: Be diligent in these matters and absorbed in them, so that your progress will be evident to all.

1TI.4.16.t: Pay close attention to your life and to your teaching. Persevere in these things, for by so doing you will save both yourself and those who hear you.
s: Pay close attention to your life and to your teaching. Persevere in these things, for by so doing you will save both yourself and those who hear you.

2CO.12.7.t: or because of these surpassingly great revelations. So to keep me from becoming conceited, I was given a thorn in my flesh, a messenger of Satan, to torment me.
s: or because of these surpassingly great revelations.
So to keep me from becoming conceited, I was given a thorn in my flesh, a messenger of Satan, to torment me.

2CO.12.8.t: Three times I pleaded with the Lord to take it away from me.
s: Three times I pleaded with the Lord to take it away from me.

2CO.12.9.t: But He said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” Therefore I will boast all the more gladly in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest on me.
s: But He said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” Therefore I will boast all the more gladly in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest on me.

2CO.12.10.t: That is why, for the sake of Christ, I delight in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions, in difficulties. For when I am weak, then I am strong.
s: That is why, for the sake of Christ, I delight in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions, in difficulties. For when I am weak, then I am strong.

COL.3.12.t: Therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, clothe yourselves with hearts of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience.
s: Therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, clothe yourselves with hearts of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience.

COL.3.13.t: Bear with one another and forgive any complaint you may have against someone else. Forgive as the Lord forgave you.
s: Bear with one another and forgive any complaint you may have against someone else. Forgive as the Lord forgave you.

COL.3.14.t: And over all these virtues put on love, which is the bond of perfect unity.
s: And over all these virtues put on love, which is the bond of perfect unity.

COL.3.15.t: Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, for to this you were called as members of one body. And be thankful.
s: Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, for to this you were called as members of one body. And be thankful.

COL.3.16.t: Let the word of Christ richly dwell within you as you teach and admonish one another with all wisdom, and as you sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs with gratitude in your hearts to God.
s: Let the word of Christ richly dwell within you as you teach and admonish one another with all wisdom, and as you sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs with gratitude in your hearts to God.

COL.3.17.t: And whatever you do, in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him.
s: And whatever you do, in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him.

COL.3.22.t: Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything, not only to please them while they are watching, but with sincerity of heart and fear of the Lord.
s: Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything, not only to please them while they are watching, but with sincerity of heart and fear of the Lord.

COL.3.23.t: Whatever you do, work at it with your whole being, for the Lord and not for men,
s: Whatever you do, work at it with your whole being, for the Lord and not for men,

COL.3.24.t: because you know that you will receive an inheritance from the Lord as your reward. It is the Lord Christ you are serving.
s: because you know that you will receive an inheritance from the Lord as your reward. It is the Lord Christ you are serving.

COL.3.25.t: Whoever does wrong will be repaid for his wrong, and there is no favoritism.
s: Whoever does wrong will be repaid for his wrong, and there is no favoritism.

COL.4.1.t: Masters, supply your slaves with what is right and fair, since you know that you also have a Master in heaven.
s: Masters, supply your slaves with what is right and fair, since you know that you also have a Master in heaven.

DEU.6.4.t: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is One.
s: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is One.

DEU.6.5.t: And you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.
s: And you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.

DEU.6.6.t: These words I am commanding you today are to be upon your hearts.
s: These words I am commanding you today are to be upon your hearts.

DEU.6.7.t: And you shall teach them diligently to your children and speak of them when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
s: And you shall teach them diligently to your children and speak of them when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.

DEU.6.8.t: Tie them as reminders on your hands and bind them on your foreheads.
s: Tie them as reminders on your hands and bind them on your foreheads.

DEU.6.9.t: Write them on the doorposts of your houses and on your gates.
s: Write them on the doorposts of your houses and on your gates.

ECC.4.7.t: Again, I saw futility under the sun.
s: Again, I saw futility under the sun.

ECC.4.8.t: There is a man all alone, without even a son or brother. And though there is no end to his labor, his eyes are still not content with his wealth: “For whom do I toil and bereave my soul of enjoyment?” This too is futile—a miserable task.
s: There is a man all alone, without even a son or brother. And though there is no end to his labor, his eyes are still not content with his wealth: “For whom do I toil and bereave my soul of enjoyment?” This too is futile—a miserable task.

ECC.4.9.t: Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their labor.
s: Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their labor.

ECC.4.10.t: For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up; but pity the one who falls without another to help him up!
s: For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up; but pity the one who falls without another to help him up!

ECC.4.11.t: Again, if two lie down together, they will keep warm; but how can one keep warm alone?
s: Again, if two lie down together, they will keep warm; but how can one keep warm alone?

ECC.4.12.t: And though one may be overpowered, two can resist. Moreover, a cord of three strands is not quickly broken.
s: And though one may be overpowered, two can resist. Moreover, a cord of three strands is not quickly broken.

ECC.9.7.t: Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a cheerful heart, for God has already approved your works:
s: Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a cheerful heart, for God has already approved your works:

ECC.9.8.t: Let your garments always be white, and never spare the oil for your head.
s: Let your garments always be white,
and never spare the oil for your head.

ECC.9.9.t: Enjoy life with your beloved wife all the days of the fleeting life that God has given you under the sun—all your fleeting days. For this is your portion in life and in your labor under the sun.
s: Enjoy life with your beloved wife all the days of the fleeting life that God has given you under the sun—all your fleeting days. For this is your portion in life and in your labor under the sun.

ECC.9.10.t: Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might, for in Sheol, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.
s: Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might, for in Sheol, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.

ECC.9.11.t: I saw something else under the sun: The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong; neither is the bread to the wise, nor the wealth to the intelligent, nor the favor to the skillful. For time and chance happen to all.
s: I saw something else under the sun: The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong; neither is the bread to the wise, nor the wealth to the intelligent, nor the favor to the skillful. For time and chance happen to all.

EPH.4.1.t: As a prisoner in the Lord, then, I urge you to walk in a manner worthy of the calling you have received:
s: As a prisoner in the Lord, then, I urge you to walk in a manner worthy of the calling you have received:

EPH.4.2.t: with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love,
s: with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love,

EPH.4.3.t: and with diligence to preserve the unity of the Spirit through the bond of peace.
s: and with diligence to preserve the unity of the Spirit through the bond of peace.

EPH.4.4.t: There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called to one hope when you were called;
s: There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called to one hope when you were called;

EPH.4.5.t: one Lord, one faith, one baptism;
s: one Lord, one faith, one baptism;

EPH.4.6.t: one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all.
s: one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all.

GAL.6.1.t: Brothers, if someone is caught in a trespass, you who are spiritual should restore him with a spirit of gentleness. But watch yourself, or you also may be tempted.
s: Brothers, if someone is caught in a trespass, you who are spiritual should restore him with a spirit of gentleness. But watch yourself, or you also may be tempted.

GAL.6.2.t: Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.
s: Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.

GAL.6.3.t: If anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself.
s: If anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself.

GAL.6.4.t: Each one should test his own work. Then he will have reason to boast in himself alone, and not in someone else.
s: Each one should test his own work. Then he will have reason to boast in himself alone, and not in someone else.

GAL.6.5.t: For each one should carry his own load.
s: For each one should carry his own load.

ISA.6.1.t: In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted; and the train of His robe filled the temple.
s: In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted; and the train of His robe filled the temple.

ISA.6.2.t: Above Him stood seraphim, each having six wings: With two wings they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they were flying.
s: Above Him stood seraphim, each having six wings: With two wings they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they were flying.

ISA.6.3.t: And they were calling out to one another: “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts; all the earth is full of His glory.”
s: And they were calling out to one another:
“Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts;
all the earth is full of His glory.”

ISA.6.4.t: At the sound of their voices the doorposts and thresholds shook, and the temple was filled with smoke.
s: At the sound of their voices the doorposts and thresholds shook, and the temple was filled with smoke.

ISA.6.5.t: Then I said: “Woe is me, for I am ruined, because I am a man of unclean lips dwelling among a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Hosts.”
s: Then I said:
“Woe is me,
for I am ruined,
because I am a man of unclean lips
dwelling among a people of unclean lips;
for my eyes have seen the King,
the LORD of Hosts.”

ISA.6.6.t: Then one of the seraphim flew to me, and in his hand was a glowing coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar.
s: Then one of the seraphim flew to me, and in his hand was a glowing coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar.

ISA.6.7.t: And with it he touched my mouth and said: “Now that this has touched your lips, your iniquity is removed and your sin is atoned for.”
s: And with it he touched my mouth and said:
“Now that this has touched your lips,
your iniquity is removed
and your sin is atoned for.”

ISA.6.8.t: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying: “Whom shall I send? Who will go for Us?” And I said: “Here am I. Send me!”
s: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying:
“Whom shall I send?
Who will go for Us?”
And I said:
“Here am I. Send me!”

ISA.40.27.t: Why do you say, O Jacob, and why do you assert, O Israel, “My way is hidden from the LORD, and my claim is ignored by my God”?
s: Why do you say, O Jacob,
and why do you assert, O Israel,
“My way is hidden from the LORD,
and my claim is ignored by my God”?

ISA.40.28.t: Do you not know? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He will not grow tired or weary; His understanding is beyond searching out.
s: Do you not know?
Have you not heard?
The LORD is the everlasting God,
the Creator of the ends of the earth.
He will not grow tired or weary;
His understanding is beyond searching out.

ISA.40.29.t: He gives power to the faint and increases the strength of the weak.
s: He gives power to the faint
and increases the strength of the weak.

ISA.40.30.t: Even youths grow tired and weary, and young men stumble and fall.
s: Even youths grow tired and weary,
and young men stumble and fall.

ISA.40.31.t: But those who wait upon the LORD will renew their strength; they will mount up with wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not faint.
s: But those who wait upon the LORD will renew their strength;
they will mount up with wings like eagles;
they will run and not grow weary,
they will walk and not faint.

ISA.41.8.t: “But you, O Israel, My servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, descendant of Abraham My friend—
s: “But you, O Israel, My servant,
Jacob, whom I have chosen,
descendant of Abraham My friend—

ISA.41.9.t: I brought you from the ends of the earth and called you from its farthest corners. I said, ‘You are My servant.’ I have chosen and not rejected you.
s: I brought you from the ends of the earth
and called you from its farthest corners.
I said, ‘You are My servant.’
I have chosen and not rejected you.

ISA.41.10.t: Do not fear, for I am with you; do not be afraid, for I am your God. I will strengthen you; I will surely help you; I will uphold you with My right hand of righteousness.
s: Do not fear, for I am with you;
do not be afraid, for I am your God.
I will strengthen you; I will surely help you;
I will uphold you with My right hand of righteousness.

ISA.41.11.t: Behold, all who rage against you will be ashamed and disgraced; those who contend with you will be reduced to nothing and will perish.
s: Behold, all who rage against you
will be ashamed and disgraced;
those who contend with you
will be reduced to nothing and will perish.

ISA.41.12.t: You will seek them but will not find them. Those who wage war against you will come to nothing.
s: You will seek them but will not find them.
Those who wage war against you will come to nothing.

ISA.41.13.t: For I am the LORD your God, who takes hold of your right hand and tells you: Do not fear, I will help you.
s: For I am the LORD your God,
who takes hold of your right hand
and tells you: Do not fear,
I will help you.

JER.1.4.t: The word of the LORD came to me, saying:
s: The word of the LORD came to me, saying:

JER.1.5.t: “Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I set you apart and appointed you as a prophet to the nations.”
s: “Before I formed you in the womb I knew you,
and before you were born I set you apart
and appointed you as a prophet to the nations.”

JER.1.6.t: “Ah, Lord GOD,” I said, “I surely do not know how to speak, for I am only a child!”
s: “Ah, Lord GOD,” I said, “I surely do not know how to speak, for I am only a child!”

JER.1.7.t: But the LORD told me: “Do not say, ‘I am only a child.’ For to everyone I send you, you must go, and all that I command you, you must speak.
s: But the LORD told me:
“Do not say,
‘I am only a child.’
For to everyone I send you,
you must go,
and all that I command you,
you must speak.

JER.1.8.t: Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you,” declares the LORD.
s: Do not be afraid of them,
for I am with you to deliver you,”
declares the LORD.

JER.1.9.t: Then the LORD reached out His hand, touched my mouth, and said to me: “Behold, I have put My words in your mouth.
s: Then the LORD reached out His hand, touched my mouth, and said to me:
“Behold, I have put My words
in your mouth.

JER.1.10.t: See, I have appointed you today over nations and kingdoms to uproot and tear down, to destroy and overthrow, to build and plant.”
s: See, I have appointed you today
over nations and kingdoms
to uproot and tear down,
to destroy and overthrow,
to build and plant.”

JHN.11.32.t: When Mary came to Jesus and saw Him, she fell at His feet and said, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.”
s: When Mary came to Jesus and saw Him, she fell at His feet and said, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.”

JHN.11.33.t: When Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her also weeping, He was deeply moved in spirit and troubled.
s: When Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her also weeping, He was deeply moved in spirit and troubled.

JHN.11.34.t: “Where have you put him?” He asked. “Come and see, Lord,” they answered.
s: “Where have you put him?” He asked.
“Come and see, Lord,” they answered.
Jesus wept.

JHN.11.36.t: Then the Jews said, “See how He loved him!”
s: Then the Jews said, “See how He loved him!”

JHN.11.37.t: But some of them asked, “Could not this man who opened the eyes of the blind also have kept Lazarus from dying?”
s: But some of them asked, “Could not this man who opened the eyes of the blind also have kept Lazarus from dying?”

JHN.15.9.t: As the Father has loved Me, so have I loved you. Remain in My love.
s: As the Father has loved Me, so have I loved you. Remain in My love.

JHN.15.10.t: If you keep My commandments, you will remain in My love, just as I have kept My Father’s commandments and remain in His love.
s: If you keep My commandments, you will remain in My love, just as I have kept My Father’s commandments and remain in His love.

JHN.15.11.t: I have told you these things so that My joy may be in you and your joy may be complete.
s: I have told you these things so that My joy may be in you and your joy may be complete.

JHN.15.12.t: This is My commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.
s: This is My commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.

JHN.15.13.t: Greater love has no one than this, that he lay down his life for his friends.
s: Greater love has no one than this, that he lay down his life for his friends.

JHN.15.14.t: You are My friends if you do what I command you.
s: You are My friends if you do what I command you.

JHN.15.15.t: No longer do I call you servants, for a servant does not understand what his master is doing. But I have called you friends, because everything I have learned from My Father I have made known to you.
s: No longer do I call you servants, for a servant does not understand what his master is doing. But I have called you friends, because everything I have learned from My Father I have made known to you.

JHN.15.16.t: You did not choose Me, but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit—fruit that will remain—so that whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you.
s: You did not choose Me, but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit—fruit that will remain—so that whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you.

JHN.15.17.t: This is My command to you: Love one another.
s: This is My command to you: Love one another.

JHN.21.9.t: When they landed, they saw a charcoal fire there with fish on it, and some bread.
s: When they landed, they saw a charcoal fire there with fish on it, and some bread.

JHN.21.10.t: Jesus told them, “Bring some of the fish you have just caught.”
s: Jesus told them, “Bring some of the fish you have just caught.”

JHN.21.11.t: So Simon Peter went aboard and dragged the net ashore. It was full of large fish, 153, but even with so many, the net was not torn.
s: So Simon Peter went aboard and dragged the net ashore. It was full of large fish, 153, but even with so many, the net was not torn.

JHN.21.12.t: “Come, have breakfast,” Jesus said to them. None of the disciples dared to ask Him, “Who are You?” They knew it was the Lord.
s: “Come, have breakfast,” Jesus said to them. None of the disciples dared to ask Him, “Who are You?” They knew it was the Lord.

JHN.21.13.t: Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and He did the same with the fish.
s: Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and He did the same with the fish.

JHN.21.14.t: This was now the third time that Jesus appeared to the disciples after He was raised from the dead.
s: This was now the third time that Jesus appeared to the disciples after He was raised from the dead.

JHN.21.15.t: When they had finished eating, Jesus asked Simon Peter, “Simon son of John, do you love Me more than these?” “Yes, Lord,” he answered, “You know I love You.” Jesus replied, “Feed My lambs.”
s: When they had finished eating, Jesus asked Simon Peter, “Simon son of John, do you love Me more than these?”
“Yes, Lord,” he answered, “You know I love You.”
Jesus replied, “Feed My lambs.”

JHN.21.16.t: Jesus asked a second time, “Simon son of John, do you love Me?” “Yes, Lord,” he answered, “You know I love You.” Jesus told him, “Shepherd My sheep.”
s: Jesus asked a second time, “Simon son of John, do you love Me?”
“Yes, Lord,” he answered, “You know I love You.”
Jesus told him, “Shepherd My sheep.”

JHN.21.17.t: Jesus asked a third time, “Simon son of John, do you love Me?” Peter was deeply hurt that Jesus had asked him a third time, “Do you love Me?” “Lord, You know all things,” he replied. “You know I love You.” Jesus said to him, “Feed My sheep.

Peter was deeply hurt that Jesus had asked him a third time, “Do you love Me?”
“Lord, You know all things,” he replied. “You know I love You.”
Jesus said to him, “Feed My sheep.

JOS.24.14.t: Now, therefore, fear the LORD and serve Him in sincerity and truth; cast aside the gods your fathers served beyond the Euphrates and in Egypt, and serve the LORD.
s: Now, therefore, fear the LORD and serve Him in sincerity and truth; cast aside the gods your fathers served beyond the Euphrates and in Egypt, and serve the LORD.

JOS.24.15.t: But if it is unpleasing in your sight to serve the LORD, then choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve, whether the gods your fathers served beyond the Euphrates, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you are living. As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD!”
s: But if it is unpleasing in your sight to serve the LORD, then choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve, whether the gods your fathers served beyond the Euphrates, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you are living. As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD!”

JOS.24.16.t: The people replied, “Far be it from us to forsake the LORD to serve other gods!
s: The people replied, “Far be it from us to forsake the LORD to serve other gods!

JOS.24.17.t: For the LORD our God brought us and our fathers out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, and performed these great signs before our eyes. He also protected us throughout our journey and among all the nations through which we traveled.
s: For the LORD our God brought us and our fathers out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, and performed these great signs before our eyes. He also protected us throughout our journey and among all the nations through which we traveled.

JOS.24.18.t: And the LORD drove out before us all the nations, including the Amorites who lived in the land. We too will serve the LORD, because He is our God!”
s: And the LORD drove out before us all the nations, including the Amorites who lived in the land. We too will serve the LORD, because He is our God!”

LUK.16.1.t: Jesus also said to His disciples, “There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his possessions.
s: Jesus also said to His disciples, “There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his possessions.

LUK.16.2.t: So he called him in to ask, ‘What is this I hear about you? Turn in an account of your management, for you cannot be manager any longer.’
s: So he called him in to ask, ‘What is this I hear about you? Turn in an account of your management, for you cannot be manager any longer.’

LUK.16.3.t: The manager said to himself, ‘What shall I do, now that my master is taking away my position? I am too weak to dig and too ashamed to beg.
s: The manager said to himself, ‘What shall I do, now that my master is taking away my position? I am too weak to dig and too ashamed to beg.

LUK.16.4.t: I know what I will do, so that after my removal from management, people will welcome me into their homes.’
s: I know what I will do, so that after my removal from management, people will welcome me into their homes.’

LUK.16.5.t: And he called in each one of his master’s debtors. ‘How much do you owe my master?’ he asked the first.
s: And he called in each one of his master’s debtors. ‘How much do you owe my master?’ he asked the first.

LUK.16.6.t: ‘A hundred measures of olive oil,’ he answered. ‘Take your bill,’ said the manager. ‘Sit down quickly, and write fifty.’
s: ‘A hundred measures of olive oil,’ he answered.
‘Take your bill,’ said the manager. ‘Sit down quickly, and write fifty.’

LUK.16.7.t: Then he asked another, ‘And how much do you owe?’ ‘A hundred measures of wheat,’ he replied. ‘Take your bill and write eighty,’ he told him.
s: Then he asked another, ‘And how much do you owe?’
‘A hundred measures of wheat,’ he replied.
‘Take your bill and write eighty,’ he told him.

LUK.16.8.t: The master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly. For the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the sons of light.
s: The master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly. For the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the sons of light.

LUK.16.9.t: I tell you, use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves, so that when it is gone, they will welcome you into eternal dwellings.
s: I tell you, use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves, so that when it is gone, they will welcome you into eternal dwellings.

LUK.16.10.t: Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
s: Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.

LUK.16.11.t: So if you have not been faithful with worldly wealth, who will entrust you with true riches?
s: So if you have not been faithful with worldly wealth, who will entrust you with true riches?

LUK.16.12.t: And if you have not been faithful with the belongings of another, who will give you belongings of your own?
s: And if you have not been faithful with the belongings of another, who will give you belongings of your own?

LUK.16.13.t: No servant can serve two masters. Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.”
s: No servant can serve two masters. Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.”

MRK.10.35.t: Then James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to Jesus and declared, “Teacher, we want You to do for us whatever we ask.”
s: Then James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to Jesus and declared, “Teacher, we want You to do for us whatever we ask.”

MRK.10.36.t: “What do you want Me to do for you?” He inquired.
s: “What do you want Me to do for you?” He inquired.

MRK.10.37.t: They answered, “Grant that one of us may sit at Your right hand and the other at Your left in Your glory.”
s: They answered, “Grant that one of us may sit at Your right hand and the other at Your left in Your glory.”

s: “You do not know what you are asking,” Jesus replied. “Can you drink the cup I will drink, or be baptized with the baptism I will undergo?”

s: “We can,” the brothers answered.
“You will drink the cup that I drink,” Jesus said, “and you will be baptized with the baptism that I undergo.

MRK.10.40.t: But to sit at My right or left is not Mine to grant. These seats belong to those for whom they have been prepared.”
s: But to sit at My right or left is not Mine to grant. These seats belong to those for whom they have been prepared.”

MRK.10.41.t: When the ten heard about this, they became indignant with James and John.
s: When the ten heard about this, they became indignant with James and John.

MRK.10.42.t: So Jesus called them together and said, “You know that those regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their superiors exercise authority over them.
s: So Jesus called them together and said, “You know that those regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their superiors exercise authority over them.

MRK.10.43.t: But it shall not be this way among you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,
s: But it shall not be this way among you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,

MRK.10.44.t: and whoever wants to be first must be the slave of all.
s: and whoever wants to be first must be the slave of all.

MRK.10.45.t: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.”
s: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.”

s: These are the proverbs of Solomon son of David,
king of Israel,

for comprehending words of insight,

PRO.1.3.t: and for receiving instruction in wise living and in righteousness, justice, and equity.
s: and for receiving instruction in wise living
and in righteousness, justice, and equity.

s: To impart prudence to the simple
and knowledge and discretion to the young,

s: let the wise listen and gain instruction,
and the discerning acquire wise counsel

PRO.1.6.t: by understanding the proverbs and parables, the sayings and riddles of the wise.
s: by understanding the proverbs and parables,
the sayings and riddles of the wise.

s: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge,
but fools despise wisdom and discipline.

s: Listen, my son, to your father’s instruction,

s: For they are a garland of grace on your head

PRO.4.20.t: My son, pay attention to my words; incline your ear to my sayings.
s: My son, pay attention to my words;
incline your ear to my sayings.

PRO.4.21.t: Do not lose sight of them; keep them within your heart.
s: Do not lose sight of them;
keep them within your heart.

PRO.4.22.t: For they are life to those who find them, and health to the whole body.
s: For they are life to those who find them,
and health to the whole body.

PRO.4.23.t: Guard your heart with all diligence, for from it flow springs of life.
s: Guard your heart with all diligence,
for from it flow springs of life.

PRO.4.24.t: Put away deception from your mouth; keep your lips from perverse speech.
s: Put away deception from your mouth;
keep your lips from perverse speech.

PRO.4.25.t: Let your eyes look forward; fix your gaze straight ahead.
s: Let your eyes look forward;
fix your gaze straight ahead.

PRO.4.26.t: Make a level path for your feet, and all your ways will be sure.
s: Make a level path for your feet,
and all your ways will be sure.

PRO.4.27.t: Do not swerve to the right or to the left; turn your feet away from evil.
s: Do not swerve to the right or to the left;
turn your feet away from evil.

PRO.6.6.t: Walk in the manner of the ant, O slacker; observe its ways and become wise.
s: Walk in the manner of the ant, O slacker;
observe its ways and become wise.

PRO.6.7.t: Without a commander, without an overseer or ruler,
s: Without a commander,
without an overseer or ruler,

PRO.6.8.t: it prepares its provisions in summer; it gathers its food at harvest.
s: it prepares its provisions in summer;
it gathers its food at harvest.

s: How long will you lie there, O slacker?
When will you get up from your sleep?

PRO.6.10.t: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest,
s: A little sleep, a little slumber,
a little folding of the hands to rest,

PRO.6.11.t: and poverty will come upon you like a robber, and need like a bandit.
s: and poverty will come upon you like a robber,
and need like a bandit.

s: With his mouth the ungodly man destroys his neighbor,
but through knowledge the righteous are rescued.

s: When the righteous thrive, the city rejoices,
and when the wicked perish, there are shouts of joy.

PRO.11.11.t: By the blessing of the upright a city is built up, but by the mouth of the wicked it is torn down.
s: By the blessing of the upright a city is built up,
but by the mouth of the wicked it is torn down.

PRO.11.12.t: Whoever shows contempt for his neighbor lacks judgment, but a man of understanding remains silent.
s: Whoever shows contempt for his neighbor lacks judgment,
but a man of understanding remains silent.

PRO.11.13.t: A gossip reveals a secret, but a trustworthy person keeps a confidence.
s: A gossip reveals a secret,
but a trustworthy person keeps a confidence.

s: For lack of guidance, a nation falls,
but with many counselors comes deliverance.

PRO.13.14.t: The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life, turning one from the snares of death.
s: The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life,
turning one from the snares of death.

PRO.13.15.t: Good understanding wins favor, but the way of the faithless is difficult.
s: Good understanding wins favor,
but the way of the faithless is difficult.

PRO.13.16.t: Every prudent man acts with knowledge, but a fool displays his folly.
s: Every prudent man acts with knowledge,
but a fool displays his folly.

PRO.13.17.t: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a faithful envoy brings healing.
s: A wicked messenger falls into trouble,
but a faithful envoy brings healing.

s: Poverty and shame come to him who ignores discipline,
but whoever heeds correction is honored.

s: Desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul,
but turning from evil is detestable to fools.

PRO.13.20.t: He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will be destroyed.
s: He who walks with the wise will become wise,
but the companion of fools will be destroyed.

s: A gentle answer turns away wrath,
but a harsh word stirs up anger.

PRO.15.2.t: The tongue of the wise commends knowledge, but the mouth of the fool spouts folly.
s: The tongue of the wise commends knowledge,
but the mouth of the fool spouts folly.

PRO.15.3.t: The eyes of the LORD are in every place, observing the evil and the good.
s: The eyes of the LORD are in every place,
observing the evil and the good.

PRO.15.4.t: A soothing tongue is a tree of life, but a perverse tongue crushes the spirit.
s: A soothing tongue is a tree of life,
but a perverse tongue crushes the spirit.

s: The plans of the heart belong to man,
but the reply of the tongue is from the LORD.

s: All a man’s ways are pure in his own eyes,
but his motives are weighed out by the LORD.

PRO.16.3.t: Commit your works to the LORD and your plans will be achieved.
s: Commit your works to the LORD
and your plans will be achieved.

s: The LORD has made everything for His purpose—
even the wicked for the day of disaster.

s: Everyone who is proud in heart is detestable to the LORD;
be assured that he will not go unpunished.

s: By loving devotion and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for,
and by the fear of the LORD one turns aside from evil.

s: When a man’s ways please the LORD,
He makes even the man’s enemies live at peace with him.

PRO.16.8.t: Better a little with righteousness than great gain with injustice.
s: Better a little with righteousness
than great gain with injustice.

PRO.16.9.t: A man’s heart plans his course, but the LORD determines his steps.
s: A man’s heart plans his course,
but the LORD determines his steps.

PRO.17.9.t: Whoever conceals an offense promotes love, but he who brings it up separates friends.
s: Whoever conceals an offense promotes love,
but he who brings it up separates friends.

PRO.17.10.t: A rebuke cuts into a man of discernment deeper than a hundred lashes cut into a fool.
s: A rebuke cuts into a man of discernment
deeper than a hundred lashes cut into a fool.

PRO.17.11.t: An evil man seeks only rebellion; a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
s: An evil man seeks only rebellion;
a cruel messenger will be sent against him.

PRO.17.12.t: It is better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool in his folly.
s: It is better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs
than a fool in his folly.

PRO.17.13.t: If anyone returns evil for good, evil will never leave his house.
s: If anyone returns evil for good,
evil will never leave his house.

s: To start a quarrel is to release a flood;
so abandon the dispute before it breaks out.

PRO.17.15.t: Acquitting the guilty and condemning the righteous— both are detestable to the LORD.
s: Acquitting the guilty and condemning the righteous—
both are detestable to the LORD.

PRO.17.16.t: Why should the fool have money in his hand with no intention of buying wisdom?
s: Why should the fool have money in his hand
with no intention of buying wisdom?

s: A friend loves at all times,

s: Better an open rebuke

s: Her children rise up and call her blessed;
her husband praises her as well:

PRO.31.29.t: “Many daughters have done noble things, but you surpass them all!”
s: “Many daughters have done noble things,
but you surpass them all!”

PRO.31.30.t: Charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.
s: Charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting,
but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.

PRO.31.31.t: Give her the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her at the gates.
s: Give her the fruit of her hands,
and let her works praise her at the gates.

PSA.9.7.t: But the LORD abides forever; He has established His throne for judgment.
s: But the LORD abides forever;
He has established His throne for judgment.

PSA.9.8.t: He judges the world with justice; He governs the people with equity.
s: He judges the world with justice;
He governs the people with equity.

PSA.9.9.t: The LORD is a refuge for the oppressed, a stronghold in times of trouble.
s: The LORD is a refuge for the oppressed,
a stronghold in times of trouble.

PSA.9.10.t: Those who know Your name trust in You, for You, O LORD, have not forsaken those who seek You.
s: Those who know Your name trust in You,
for You, O LORD, have not forsaken those who seek You.

PSA.9.11.t: Sing praises to the LORD, who dwells in Zion; proclaim His deeds among the nations.
s: Sing praises to the LORD, who dwells in Zion;
proclaim His deeds among the nations.

PSA.9.12.t: For the Avenger of bloodshed remembers; He does not ignore the cry of the afflicted.
s: For the Avenger of bloodshed remembers;
He does not ignore the cry of the afflicted.

PSA.10.12.t: Arise, O LORD! Lift up Your hand, O God! Do not forget the helpless.
s: Arise, O LORD! Lift up Your hand, O God!
Do not forget the helpless.

PSA.10.13.t: Why has the wicked man renounced God? He says to himself, “You will never call me to account.”
s: Why has the wicked man renounced God?
He says to himself, “You will never call me to account.”

PSA.10.14.t: But You have regarded trouble and grief; You see to repay it by Your hand. The victim entrusts himself to You; You are the helper of the fatherless.
s: But You have regarded trouble and grief;
You see to repay it by Your hand.
The victim entrusts himself to You;
You are the helper of the fatherless.

PSA.10.15.t: Break the arm of the wicked and evildoer; call him to account for his wickedness until none is left to be found.
s: Break the arm of the wicked and evildoer;
call him to account for his wickedness
until none is left to be found.

PSA.10.16.t: The LORD is King forever and ever; the nations perish from His land.
s: The LORD is King forever and ever;
the nations perish from His land.

PSA.10.17.t: You have heard, O LORD, the desire of the humble; You will strengthen their hearts. You will incline Your ear,
s: You have heard, O LORD, the desire of the humble;
You will strengthen their hearts.
You will incline Your ear,

PSA.10.18.t: to vindicate the fatherless and oppressed, that the men of the earth may strike terror no more.
s: to vindicate the fatherless and oppressed,
that the men of the earth
may strike terror no more.

PSA.34.17.t: The righteous cry out, and the LORD hears; He delivers them from all their troubles.
s: The righteous cry out, and the LORD hears;
He delivers them from all their troubles.

PSA.34.18.t: The LORD is near to the brokenhearted; He saves the contrite in spirit.
s: The LORD is near to the brokenhearted;
He saves the contrite in spirit.

PSA.34.19.t: Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but the LORD delivers him from them all.
s: Many are the afflictions of the righteous,
but the LORD delivers him from them all.

PSA.37.23.t: The steps of a man are ordered by the LORD who takes delight in his journey.
s: The steps of a man are ordered by the LORD
who takes delight in his journey.

PSA.37.24.t: Though he falls, he will not be overwhelmed, for the LORD is holding his hand.
s: Though he falls, he will not be overwhelmed,
for the LORD is holding his hand.

PSA.37.25.t: I once was young and now am old, yet never have I seen the righteous abandoned or their children begging for bread.
s: I once was young and now am old,
yet never have I seen the righteous abandoned
or their children begging for bread.

PSA.37.26.t: They are ever generous and quick to lend, and their children are a blessing.
s: They are ever generous and quick to lend,
and their children are a blessing.

PSA.41.1.t: Blessed is the one who cares for the poor; the LORD will deliver him in the day of trouble.
s: Blessed is the one who cares for the poor;
the LORD will deliver him in the day of trouble.
PSA.41.1.h: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David.

PSA.41.2.t: The LORD will protect and preserve him; He will bless him in the land and refuse to surrender him to the will of his foes.
s: The LORD will protect and preserve him;
He will bless him in the land
and refuse to surrender him
to the will of his foes.

PSA.41.3.t: The LORD will sustain him on his bed of illness and restore him from his bed of sickness.
s: The LORD will sustain him on his bed of illness
and restore him from his bed of sickness.

PSA.41.4.t: I said, “O LORD, be gracious to me; heal me, for I have sinned against You.”
s: I said, “O LORD, be gracious to me;
heal me, for I have sinned against You.”

PSA.42.5.t: Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the unease within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him for the salvation of His presence.
s: Why are you downcast, O my soul?
Why the unease within me?
Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him
for the salvation of His presence.

PSA.42.6.t: O my God, my soul despairs within me. Therefore I remember You from the land of Jordan and the peaks of Hermon— even from Mount Mizar.
s: O my God, my soul despairs within me.
Therefore I remember You
from the land of Jordan and the peaks of Hermon—
even from Mount Mizar.

PSA.42.7.t: Deep calls to deep in the roar of Your waterfalls; all Your breakers and waves have rolled over me.
s: Deep calls to deep
in the roar of Your waterfalls;
all Your breakers and waves
have rolled over me.

PSA.42.8.t: The LORD decrees His loving devotion by day, and at night His song is with me as a prayer to the God of my life.
s: The LORD decrees His loving devotion by day,
and at night His song is with me
as a prayer to the God of my life.

PSA.42.9.t: I say to God my Rock, “Why have You forgotten me? Why must I walk in sorrow because of the enemy’s oppression?”
s: I say to God my Rock,
“Why have You forgotten me?
Why must I walk in sorrow
because of the enemy’s oppression?”

PSA.42.10.t: Like the crushing of my bones, my enemies taunt me, while they say to me all day long, “Where is your God?”
s: Like the crushing of my bones,
my enemies taunt me,
while they say to me all day long,
“Where is your God?”

PSA.42.11.t: Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the unease within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him, my Savior and my God.
s: Why are you downcast, O my soul?
Why the unease within me?
Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him,
my Savior and my God.

PSA.90.12.t: So teach us to number our days, that we may present a heart of wisdom.
s: So teach us to number our days,
that we may present a heart of wisdom.

PSA.90.13.t: Return, O LORD! How long will it be? Have compassion on Your servants.
s: Return, O LORD! How long will it be?
Have compassion on Your servants.

PSA.90.14.t: Satisfy us in the morning with Your loving devotion, that we may sing for joy and be glad all our days.
s: Satisfy us in the morning with Your loving devotion,
that we may sing for joy and be glad all our days.

PSA.90.15.t: Make us glad for as many days as You have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen evil.
s: Make us glad for as many days as You have afflicted us,
for as many years as we have seen evil.

PSA.90.16.t: May Your work be shown to Your servants, and Your splendor to their children.
s: May Your work be shown to Your servants,
and Your splendor to their children.

PSA.90.17.t: May the favor of the Lord our God rest upon us; establish for us the work of our hands— yes, establish the work of our hands!
s: May the favor of the Lord our God rest upon us;
establish for us the work of our hands—
yes, establish the work of our hands!

PSA.103.13.t: As a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion on those who fear Him.
s: As a father has compassion on his children,
so the LORD has compassion on those who fear Him.

PSA.103.14.t: For He knows our frame; He is mindful that we are dust.
s: For He knows our frame;
He is mindful that we are dust.

PSA.103.15.t: As for man, his days are like grass— he blooms like a flower of the field;
s: As for man, his days are like grass—
he blooms like a flower of the field;

PSA.103.16.t: when the wind passes over, it vanishes, and its place remembers it no more.
s: when the wind passes over, it vanishes,
and its place remembers it no more.

PSA.103.17.t: But from everlasting to everlasting the loving devotion of the LORD extends to those who fear Him, and His righteousness to their children’s children—
s: But from everlasting to everlasting
the loving devotion of the LORD
extends to those who fear Him,
and His righteousness to their children’s children—

PSA.103.18.t: to those who keep His covenant and remember to obey His precepts.
s: to those who keep His covenant
and remember to obey His precepts.

PSA.133.1.t: Behold, how good and pleasant it is when brothers live together in harmony!
s: Behold, how good and pleasant it is
when brothers live together in harmony!
PSA.133.1.h: A song of ascents. Of David.

PSA.133.2.t: It is like fine oil on the head, running down on the beard, running down Aaron’s beard over the collar of his robes.
s: It is like fine oil on the head,
running down on the beard,
running down Aaron’s beard
over the collar of his robes.

PSA.133.3.t: It is like the dew of Hermon falling on the mountains of Zion. For there the LORD has bestowed the blessing of life forevermore.
s: It is like the dew of Hermon
falling on the mountains of Zion.
For there the LORD has bestowed the blessing
of life forevermore.

PSA.147.1.t: Hallelujah! How good it is to sing praises to our God, how pleasant and lovely to praise Him!
s: Hallelujah!
How good it is to sing praises to our God,
how pleasant and lovely to praise Him!

PSA.147.2.t: The LORD builds up Jerusalem; He gathers the exiles of Israel.
s: The LORD builds up Jerusalem;
He gathers the exiles of Israel.

PSA.147.3.t: He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.
s: He heals the brokenhearted
and binds up their wounds.

PSA.147.4.t: He determines the number of the stars; He calls them each by name.
s: He determines the number of the stars;
He calls them each by name.

PSA.147.5.t: Great is our Lord, and mighty in power; His understanding has no limit.
s: Great is our Lord, and mighty in power;
His understanding has no limit.

PSA.147.6.t: The LORD sustains the humble, but casts the wicked to the ground.
s: The LORD sustains the humble,
but casts the wicked to the ground.

PSA.147.7.t: Sing to the LORD with thanksgiving; make music on the harp to our God,
s: Sing to the LORD with thanksgiving;
make music on the harp to our God,

PSA.147.8.t: who covers the sky with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who makes grass to grow on the hills.
s: who covers the sky with clouds,
who prepares rain for the earth,
who makes grass to grow on the hills.

PSA.147.9.t: He provides food for the animals, and for the young ravens when they call.
s: He provides food for the animals,
and for the young ravens when they call.

PSA.147.10.t: He does not delight in the strength of the horse; He takes no pleasure in the legpower of the man.
s: He does not delight in the strength of the horse;
He takes no pleasure in the legpower of the man.

PSA.147.11.t: The LORD is pleased with those who fear Him, who hope in His loving devotion.
s: The LORD is pleased with those who fear Him,
who hope in His loving devotion.

REV.21.1.t: Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and earth had passed away, and the sea was no more.
s: Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and earth had passed away, and the sea was no more.

REV.21.2.t: I saw the holy city, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.
s: I saw the holy city, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.

REV.21.3.t: And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying: “Behold, the dwelling place of God is with man, and He will dwell with them. They will be His people, and God Himself will be with them as their God.
s: And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying:
“Behold, the dwelling place of God is with man,
and He will dwell with them.
They will be His people,
and God Himself will be with them as their God.

REV.21.4.t: ‘He will wipe away every tear from their eyes,’ and there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the former things have passed away.”
s: ‘He will wipe away every tear from their eyes,’
and there will be no more death
or mourning or crying or pain,
for the former things have passed away.”

REV.21.5.t: And the One seated on the throne said, “Behold, I make all things new.” Then He said, “Write this down, for these words are faithful and true.”
s: And the One seated on the throne said, “Behold, I make all things new.” Then He said, “Write this down, for these words are faithful and true.”

ROM.12.9.t: Love must be sincere. Detest what is evil; cling to what is good.
s: Love must be sincere. Detest what is evil; cling to what is good.

ROM.12.10.t: Be devoted to one another in brotherly love. Outdo yourselves in honoring one another.
s: Be devoted to one another in brotherly love. Outdo yourselves in honoring one another.

ROM.12.11.t: Do not let your zeal subside; keep your spiritual fervor, serving the Lord.
s: Do not let your zeal subside; keep your spiritual fervor, serving the Lord.

ROM.12.12.t: Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, persistent in prayer.
s: Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, persistent in prayer.

ROM.12.13.t: Share with the saints who are in need. Practice hospitality.
s: Share with the saints who are in need. Practice hospitality.

ROM.12.14.t: Bless those who persecute you. Bless and do not curse.
s: Bless those who persecute you. Bless and do not curse.

ROM.12.15.t: Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.
s: Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.

ROM.12.16.t: Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but enjoy the company of the lowly. Do not be conceited.
s: Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but enjoy the company of the lowly. Do not be conceited.

ROM.12.17.t: Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Carefully consider what is right in the eyes of everybody.
s: Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Carefully consider what is right in the eyes of everybody.

ROM.12.18.t: If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone.
s: If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone.

ROM.12.19.t: Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for God’s wrath. For it is written: “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”
s: Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for God’s wrath. For it is written: “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”

ROM.12.20.t: On the contrary, “If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink. For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head.”
s: On the contrary,
“If your enemy is hungry, feed him;
if he is thirsty, give him a drink.
For in so doing,
you will heap burning coals on his head.”

ROM.12.21.t: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
s: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

ROM.13.6.t: This is also why you pay taxes. For the authorities are God’s servants, who devote themselves to their work.
s: This is also why you pay taxes. For the authorities are God’s servants, who devote themselves to their work.

ROM.13.7.t: Pay everyone what you owe him: taxes to whom taxes are due, revenue to whom revenue is due, respect to whom respect is due, honor to whom honor is due.
s: Pay everyone what you owe him: taxes to whom taxes are due, revenue to whom revenue is due, respect to whom respect is due, honor to whom honor is due.

ROM.13.8.t: Be indebted to no one, except to one another in love. For he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.
s: Be indebted to no one, except to one another in love. For he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.

ROM.13.9.t: The commandments “Do not commit adultery,” “Do not murder,” “Do not steal,” “Do not covet,” and any other commandments, are summed up in this one decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”
s: The commandments “Do not commit adultery,” “Do not murder,” “Do not steal,” “Do not covet,” and any other commandments, are summed up in this one decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”

ROM.13.10.t: Love does no wrong to its neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.
s: Love does no wrong to its neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.

SNG.2.1.t: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valley.
s: I am a rose of Sharon,
a lily of the valley.

SNG.2.2.t: Like a lily among the thorns is my darling among the maidens.
s: Like a lily among the thorns
is my darling among the maidens.

SNG.2.3.t: Like an apricot tree among the trees of the forest is my beloved among the young men. I delight to sit in his shade, and his fruit is sweet to my taste.
s: Like an apricot tree among the trees of the forest
is my beloved among the young men.
I delight to sit in his shade,
and his fruit is sweet to my taste.

SNG.2.4.t: He has brought me to the house of wine, and his banner over me is love.
s: He has brought me to the house of wine,
and his banner over me is love.

SNG.2.5.t: Sustain me with raisins; refresh me with apples, for I am faint with love.
s: Sustain me with raisins;
refresh me with apples,
for I am faint with love.

SNG.2.6.t: His left hand is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.
s: His left hand is under my head,
and his right arm embraces me.

SNG.2.7.t: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right.
s: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you
by the gazelles and does of the field:
Do not arouse or awaken love
until the time is right.

SNG.8.5.t: Who is this coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? I roused you under the apple tree; there your mother conceived you; there she travailed and brought you forth.
s: Who is this coming up from the wilderness,
leaning on her beloved?
I roused you under the apple tree;
there your mother conceived you;
there she travailed and brought you forth.

SNG.8.6.t: Set me as a seal over your heart, as a seal upon your arm. For love is as strong as death, its jealousy as unrelenting as Sheol. Its sparks are fiery flames, the fiercest blaze of all.
s: Set me as a seal over your heart,
as a seal upon your arm.
For love is as strong as death,
its jealousy as unrelenting as Sheol.
Its sparks are fiery flames,
the fiercest blaze of all.

SNG.8.7.t: Mighty waters cannot quench love; rivers cannot sweep it away. If a man were to give all the wealth of his house for love, his offer would be utterly scorned.
s: Mighty waters cannot quench love;
rivers cannot sweep it away.
If a man were to give all the wealth of his house for love,
his offer would be utterly scorned.
